pcs.pc_description: identify the method of calibration, as requested in the Job Order, of different parameters such as AC/DC voltage sources, AC/DC current sources, function generators and other similar instruments, etc.
identify the comparison methods to be used (such as Difference Method, Null Method, Substitution Method, Direct/Automated Method etc.)

create an observation sheet and record the details of the UUC (company name, lab reference number, type, make, model, serial number, date, time, technician's name, etc.) as per the standard form/format specified in the SOP
ensure that while performing calibration to achieve Calibration and measurement capability (CMC), Test uncertainty Ratio (TUR) of preferably 3:1 must be followed
verify that the UUC is defect-free, i.e. it has no sign of physical damage, has readable markings, is clean

identify the reference instruments and components (i.e. divider, Digital multimeter, Oscilloscope, Multifunction Calibrator etc.) to use for the parameter measurements and ensure their functionalities
connect the reference equipment, the UUC and any other accessories as per the recommended configuration norms and method of calibration
select appropriate functions, parameters and range for the reference equipment and UUC
set up the recommended automation environment, if the measurements are automated, enable the software and enter the required configuration parameters as per the SOP documents
observe and record the readings of ambient temperature and relative humidity using recommended devices before calibration
ensure the reference equipment and the UUC has stabilised after calibration, as recommended by the manufacturer or the SOP
use hand gloves of specified material and any other handling SOP specified for handling the Unit Under Calibration (UUC)

identify parameters to measure, calculate the chosen parameters for the number of times as specified in the SOP document using the UUC and reference instruments and record the readings/observations of each calculation
perform the required calibration steps in a sequence and in case the measurements are automated, then ensure that the steps monitored on the HMI (computer display) are occurring as per SOP
use appropriate software/application for recording readings and messages in case of automated calculations of parameters
calculate the value of parameters from the true value by taking temperature and humidity error into account
select the calculation equation(s) for the type of calibration to be performed after referring to the SOP and the appropriate NOS
use the form/format specified in the SOP for performing calculations and recording observations
perform the required calculations using calculator (manually) or software (automated) as specified in the SOP for specific parameters

perform Type 'A' and Type ‘B’ uncertainty calculations based on measurement data as per SOP (estimation of measurement uncertainty such as U1 Uncertainty reported in the calibration certificate of the standard(s) / master(s), U2 Uncertainty arising from stability data of the measurement standard(s) / master(s) used for calibration, U3: Uncertainty from the resolution of the UUC, and so on)
record the results of calculations, including uncertainty, in the specified format
prepare post-calibration report in the format specified in the SOP and share the report with the designated persons/supervisor
return the reference instruments and accessories to their recommended storage conditions and positions
return the UUC to its recommended storage condition
fix/attach any recommended tag/markings on the UUC to signify that its calibration has been done

modules.module_title: analyse general calibration requirements to ensure presence of an optimal environment

pcs.pc_description: inspect the central air conditioning plants and other external factors to assess the temperature of the area/laboratory
inspect the room/area for any abnormal noise in the calibration area and assess the source of vibration in case felt (refer to SOP for acceptable noise level—usually less than 60dba)

check for lighting/ associated electrical equipment in the calibration installation area and match it with the recommended level of illumination (typically, 250- 500 Lux on the working table, or as specified in the SOP documents)
check for temporary/unsafe electrical wiring that may be put calibration in jeopardy
check for ambient temperature and humidity in the calibration area as specified in the SOP documents
inspect the environment parameters to analyse if they may adversely affect the required accuracy of measurement and report to the supervisor in case discrepancies are detected

check that the SOP norms for intensity and location of magnetic field sources, such as transformers, looped wires, ferrous materials, etc., in order to minimise magnetic interference in the measurements, especially for magnetic measurements such as inductor, etc.
ensure that Electromagnetic interference (EMI) and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) norms are to be followed as per SOP for emission and immunity testing

ensure earthing norms are correctly followed for power supply, AC/DC mains and entire circuitry as per SOP in accordance with relevant specification (as per IS:3043 general standards earth resistance should be less than 1 ohm and earth to neutral voltage should be less than 1 volt)
inspect the calibration area/laboratory to ensure it is free from dust and external air pressure, and positive air pressure is normally maintained inside the laboratory to avoid ingress of dust
assess possible treatment to be given, as per standards and first-aid guidelines specified in the organizational documents, for electric shock

ensure that a wall chart listing emergency helpline numbers, steps to take for treatment of electric shock and proper first-aid procedure for the same is placed near the power supply switchgear and at other prominent places (as prescribed under Indian Electricity Rules 1956)

modules.module_title: inspect equipment, instruments and system required for calibration

pcs.pc_description: check proper and correct RF/Microwave (1 GHz and Above), time and frequency (LF and HF, Time interval, Time Period) and temperature simulation are as per SOP documents
ensure that the power supply, usually from a UPS, is as per standards (e.g. ensure correct voltage, frequency, Total Harmonic Distortion or THD, transients, regulation, etc. are all as per SOP values
check that any installed isolation transformers, filters, etc. are not tampered with and the “hum” interference is within standard limits

assess the operation of heavy loads in the premises or nearby locations to ensure it does not cause any dip in voltage or transient currents that may adversely affect calibration and report any concerns to the relevant department
check for availability of instruments in the Electrotechnical Metrology Calibration setup

analyse requirements and arrange for protective measures, such as transient suppressors, to ensure that the laboratory is prepared for high current spikes and transients emanating from operation of heavy machines, surges in power supply and other such reasons
